**Finding: deviation (WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration)**

**What the document does well.** Section 7.3 gives Corio a genuine express warranty from Commerce One — substantial conformance to the Documentation, defect-free media, and no willfully introduced malicious code — and Section 7.4 adds a Y2K warranty. The remedy paragraph (p0079) delivers correction, then replacement free of charge, and termination with a refund of all prepaid fees where the breach cannot be corrected at Commerce One's expense. The disclaimer at p0084 is limited to implied warranties and does not swallow the express warranties. Section 11.2 also makes post-Warranty-Period spec compliance a material condition.

**Why it still fails the fallback.** The single material defect is duration. The Warranty Period is only **sixty (60) days from the Effective Date**, hard-capped at **December 31, 1999** — yet Acceptance Testing under Section 3.1 may itself run until December 31, 1999. The warranty can therefore lapse on or even before the date we accept the Software, leaving no conformance cover. That is below the playbook fallback of ninety (90) days for software.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** A single minimal edit to p0078:

- Delete: "sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, but in no event not later than December 31, 1999"
- Insert: "twelve (12) months from the date of Corio's acceptance of the Software pursuant to Section 3.1"

The remedy, benefit-of-Corio language and the two exclusions in (a)–(b) are left untouched, so the edit changes only the term we need.

**Comment lodged.** "[Playbook] We extended the Warranty Period to twelve (12) months running from acceptance rather than sixty (60) days from the Effective Date with a fixed December 31, 1999 cut-off, since a period that can expire before or shortly after acceptance testing leaves us without a conformance warranty. Our playbook position is 12 months for software; we can accept ninety (90) days from acceptance as a fallback, and the existing correct/replace/refund remedy is unchanged."

Because the remedy limb already meets the playbook and Section 11.2 carries conformance obligations beyond the Warranty Period, the 90-days-from-acceptance fallback is a realistic landing zone if Commerce One resists 12 months.
